explanation:
[EFFECT] Clear weather (category 1) gives a small positive boost to predicted rentals, while mist or cloud (category 2) has a near-neutral effect. The biggest drop occurs at light rain or snow (category 3), where predicted demand is substantially reduced — SHAP values fall as low as −0.65 in log space, meaning rentals can be cut by more than half. Heavy rain (category 4) has very few observations, so its estimated effect is uncertain, but it does not appear worse than category 3 based on the available data.

[IMPORTANCE] With a global importance score of 0.051 and a rank of 7 out of 9 features, weather situation is one of the weaker predictors in this model — other factors such as hour of day or temperature have a much larger overall influence on demand.

[RECOMMENDATION] When light rain or snow is forecast, plan for meaningfully fewer rentals and consider reducing bike redistribution effort or staffing at stations, as the model consistently predicts a large drop in demand under those conditions.
